etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English proposen, from Anglo-Norman proposer (verb), propos (noun), Middle French proposer (verb) , propos (noun), from Latin prōpōnō, prōpōnere, with conjugation altered based on poser. Doublet of propound.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To suggest a plan, course of action, etc.

quote.text:
President Moon Jae-in proposed the plan this week during a meeting with government officials, his spokesman said.
Audio (US):(file)

definitions.definition: (intransitive, sometimes followed by to) To ask for a person's hand in marriage.
